title: Accelerator bastionless nodepool orchestration Terraform module for Private VPC
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU-backed nodepools inside customer Private VPCs that can operate without a bastion host for orchestration. The module must support both ASG-style managed instance groups and Karpenter-style demand-based provisioning, provide safe upgrade paths for NVIDIA/AMD drivers and CUDA runtimes, and implement healthchecks and graceful rotation hooks suitable for high-throughput inference workloads.

Background: Customers running Redwood Private do not want to expose bastion hosts or additional jump boxes. Current nodepool modules assume SSH access for manual remediation and upgrades. To support fully bastionless operations we need infrastructure-level hooks (lifecycle hooks, SQS/CloudWatch events, instance tags), Kubernetes-side drain coordination, and a small control-plane agent pattern (handoff controller) to orchestrate safe upgrades and scale-ins.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the control-plane agent itself end-to-end (that is tracked in ENG-847400). It focuses on the Terraform surface, cloud-native lifecycle hooks, IAM, networking, and the initial set of scripts/configmaps that the agent will consume.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for: desired_gpu_type, gpu_count_per_node, node_tier_profile, scaling_policy (asg|karpenter), prewarm_capacity, maintenance_window
Module creates ASG lifecycle hooks (or Karpenter provisioner annotations) that trigger SNS/SQS messages for a rotation pipeline
Healthcheck Lambda (or equivalent) can mark instances as healthy/unhealthy via instance tags and set Kubernetes node readiness accordingly
Driver upgrade workflow performs staggered cordon+drain with a configurable drain_timeout and verifies inference pods (probe-based) are rescheduled before terminating nodes
No Terraform plan requires open SSH ingress rules into customer VPCs; all agent communication uses VPC-native messaging or node-to-control-plane outbound connections
Automated canary: when release=true, module can create a small canary nodepool (configurable size) that validates bootstrapping and driver installation before promoting to full pool
tasks: Design input/output schema and examples (variables.tf docs)
Implement ASG + lifecycle hooks template and IAM role for hook processor
Add Karpenter Provisioner config generation with nodeSelector and startupScripts
Create healthcheck Lambda/daemonset examples and Terraform provisioners for secrets/keys
Write driver upgrade bootstrap scripts and example Conftest policy for safe rollouts
Add module tests: terratest to create a small VPC + nodepool in CI and validate scaling hooks
Document runbooks and upgrade checklist in confluence and link from module README

notes:
Design trade-offs:
- Using lifecycle hooks and SQS gives us a decoupled system for safe rotation without SSH, but requires reliable message processing.
- Karpenter offers better bin-packing and lower cost for bursty inference; ASG remains important for guaranteed reserved capacity customers. The module supports both and standardizes the handoff signals.
- The canary nodepool mode adds ~3–5 minute boot latency on initial deployment but catches AMI/driver regressions early.
Implementation checklist: variables/docs -> terraform resources/templates -> test harness -> docs + runbooks.
